summary: Built the brief-3 national catalog backend and the shared contracts. M1: every §14.1-14.7/14.12 pydantic model (all additions defaulted), web/src/api types, getGeoLookup/getAccuracyRegions/state option, records.ts (recordIssuerLabel, recordBlocks) with tests, summaryFixture, SPEC §5.1/§6 rows, contracts<->types.ts parity test. M2: fire3d/regions.py with public-domain TIGERweb states/counties and BTS NTAD time zones (+ Navajo Nation/Hopi), GET /api/geo/lookup, standard UTM zones 10-19 (California unchanged), check_bundle, fixture-east (NC, UTM 17, America/New_York). M3: sources/wfigs.py and the national list in catalog.py (CAL FIRE the record in California, CA_ACTIVE_RULE 'either', CA_COMPLEX_ROWS 'calfire', duplicates, POOState rule, RX/CX/AK/HI excluded, ids from IRWIN + UFI year, resolve_listed/get_summary/find_by_irwin/is_supported/record_issuer, sources[], WFIGS-down and CAL FIRE-down fallbacks, default year = current UTC year, state= filter, gzip, build-gate texts), national FIRMS loaders (load_live_us/load_year_us with pyarrow filters, firms_us_{year}.parquet; CA wrappers deprecated) with every caller in my files switched, national live loop and LiveStatus.detections_24h; recorded WFIGS/CAL FIRE/FIRMS samples and the merge regression set. M4: GET /api/official/incident-record (api/records.py) and GET /api/accuracy-regions with the OSCC seed. M5: national gazetteer (places, counties, ZIP areas) and national geocode parsing/fields. Cut line: (a) ZCTA+county rows, (b) ca_county_gacc.json, (d) SPEC prose, (e) nwcg_agency_codes.json (PMS 931, public domain), (f) id pinning are done; (c) KD-tree not done (dense matching 0.57 s on a 235 x 11,792 national case). Live check on API 8711: 235 active fires in 23 states, 2026 list 1,192, 2025 list 856, gzip 13.5 %, detections_24h 10,816 (CA 199).

contract_deviations: §14.1 before-validator is a model_validator(mode='after') using model_fields_set (same effect): a mode='before' validator makes strict JSON validation reject every JSON array as a tuple (bbox_lonlat), which broke contract_problems(IncidentListResponse, ...).

§14.3 coverage_at uses a 1 km tolerance, not 5 km: the TIGERweb state polygons already include near-shore water, and 5 km would put central Tijuana (2.0 km from the border; required outside_us) and Windsor, ON (2.8 km) in the US. state_at keeps max_km=5 and time_zone_at the 5 km nearest-zone rule.

§14.2 duplicates: sizes must both be reported and over 1 ac (two different tiny same-named fires are never merged, so no active fire is hidden); duplicates are removed before the California merge (TCU then has 5 members).
§14.2 a CAL FIRE fire matched by two WFIGS records (Dale: DALE and BRADFORD BRANCH) keeps both in other_records and takes the irwin_id of the same-name record (null when there is no single one).
§14.2 id pinning tested with a synthetic before/after pair (no recorded pair exists).
§14.4 seed has no 'fires' and no 'fuels_editions' (per-fire era5_hours unknown; never guessed); OSCC growth_sorensen stored as 0.433 (renders 0.43).
Alaska/Hawaii/territory WFIGS ids resolve through resolve_listed (with their own state and zone, e.g. America/Anchorage) although never listed, so the build gate answers 422 instead of 404.
WFIGS year lists are never fetched below 100 ac (WFIGS_YEAR_FLOOR_ACRES); min_acres below that lists CAL FIRE of every size plus WFIGS >= 100 ac.
geocode: Census names are kept ('Boise, ID' -> 'Boise City, ID', exact through the alias 'Boise'); local match 'name' carries ', ST' as §14.10 says.

§14.5 (review round 1, R3): a California row matched to several NIFC WFIGS records, none of them with its name (irwin_id null), answers not_covered with 'NIFC WFIGS lists this fire under several records ({names}), so no single record is shown here.' instead of 'NIFC WFIGS has no record matched to this fire.' The integration should add this case to §14.5.

A California WFIGS id that the merge folds into a CAL FIRE fire is not resolvable by resolve_listed unless a bundle exists under it (then id pinning applies); otherwise an old link is served read-only from its manifest.

Codes PMS 931 does not name (INTER, SHP, TRIBE, USMC) stay verbatim in labels; 'C&L' reads 'County and Local'.
The live list matches California rows against CAL FIRE's year lists of the WFIGS rows' years and the year before (cached 30 min / 24 h by fire3d.http).

fixes_round_1.R1: fixed. Verified: summary_changes copied only SUMMARY_SYNC_FIELDS, so a bundle built under a WFIGS id that CAL FIRE lists later got CAL FIRE's acres, update time and url under record_source 'wfigs', record_issuer '<CODE> via NIFC WFIGS' and the IRWIN uid. Now api/live.py record_identity(summary) = (record_source, uid) (uid upper case without braces; old manifests default to ('calfire', calfire_uid)); when it differs between the bundle summary and the fresh row, summary_changes also copies RECORD_IDENTITY_FIELDS (name, source_name, record_source, record_issuer, uid, calfire_uid, agency, agency_code, unique_fire_id, aliases, complex_name, state, time_zone, started_ms, year). The id, time_origin_ms and built_ms stay. I added started_ms and year to the list the review gave, because refresh_live writes the whole fresh row anyway and the start time is the record's own number too. Tests: test_us_catalog_list.py::test_id_pinning_keeps_the_bundle_id (the McCovey before/after pair: after one sync the issuer, uid, calfire_uid, url, acres, name, agency, aliases and start come from CAL FIRE, the id stays, the summary passes the contract, and a second sync changes nothing) and test_live_housekeeping.py::test_summary_changes_copy_the_record_identity_only_when_the_record_changes (the same record leaves the identity fields alone; a pre-brief-3 manifest is treated as the same CAL FIRE record; the change works the other way too; a braced, lower-case IRWIN id counts as the same record).

fixes_round_1.R3: fixed, with a recorded contract deviation. Verified: a CAL FIRE row matched to two or more WFIGS records, none of them with its name, has irwin_id null (catalog.enrich_calfire), so the endpoint said 'NIFC WFIGS has no record matched to this fire.' Now, when irwin_id is null and other_records holds two or more NIFC WFIGS records, the answer is not_covered with 'NIFC WFIGS lists this fire under several records ({names}), so no single record is shown here.' The names are verbatim and joined by ', ' (records.several_reason). No match keeps the contract's wording. I did not use the review's 'each linked from the fire's records': the fire card (recordBlocks) shows an other_records entry only when its active status differs, so that claim would not always be true. Test: test_us_catalog_records.py::test_calfire_row_with_several_records. Recorded in contract3/us-catalog.md Deviations so the integration can add it to §14.5.
